messages.author: 79cbcdf70bb4b9c6
messages.subject: possible bug involving automatic differentiation
parts:
Dear all,

I think I've found a rather strange bug which might have to do with automatic differentiation. The model below just expresses an IID N(0,1) vector x[1] ... x[n] but in the model part the distance matrix d_ij = |x[i] - x[j]| is computed. By definition d_ii = 0, so this part is invariant to the value of x. The distance matrix is *not* used to update the log probability of the model so it should play no role. Sampling fails with:

Error : No acceptably small step size could be found. Perhaps the posterior is not continuous?

which I'm guessing comes from a 0 derivative, but why should that happen?


Here's the code:
-------------------

data {
int<lower=1> n;
}
parameters {
vector[n] x;
}
model {
matrix[n,n] D;
//Prior
for (i in 1:n)
{  
    x[i] ~ normal(0,1);
}

//Compute distance matrix
for (i in 1:n)
{
for (j in i:n) //no error when using j in (i+1):n
 {
 D[i,j] <- sqrt(square(x[i]-x[j]));
 //Note: no error when using fabs instead of sqrt(square(.))
 } 
}

}
-------------

See session info below. Thanks!

Best

Simon Barthelme
